nodes.title: Upsert/REPLACE/MERGE on a globally unique key mutates the other tenant's row: 261/300 (PG 17.11, 19rc1, SQLite 3.45.3)
nodes.summary: ON CONFLICT (id) DO UPDATE (even SET x only), INSERT OR REPLACE / REPLACE INTO, MERGE ON t.id=s.id all leak 261/300 with global PK; UPDATE OR REPLACE SET id=collide 112/300 (SQLite). Hardened: composite PK (tenant,id) 0, DO UPDATE .. WHERE t.tenant=excluded.tenant 0 (silent no-op), MERGE ON also tenant 0 leaks but 261 unique-violation errors (existence oracle, bytebase footgun #12). MySQL docs: ON DUPLICATE KEY updates one row when several unique indexes match.
nodes.specifics: repro in repro.sql; ops op_upsert_global_all/x/guarded/composite in wp_run.py
nodes.overclaim_risk: real schemas with composite PK are immune; risk is schema-dependent

nodes.title: UPDATE that sets the tenant column: 113/300 sqlite, 110/300 PG leak; hardened SET tenant=handle 0; RLS good policy blocks 110/110
nodes.summary: Row leaves scope (post-image W2). Native: RLS WITH CHECK, sqlite authorizer deny SQLITE_UPDATE t.tenant (blocks all 300, static). Partitioned (hash) parent row movement under RLS still blocked (ExecCrossPartitionUpdate deletes then reinserts via root, re-checking).

nodes.title: RLS WITH CHECK(true) / UPDATE USING(true) misconfig is masked when WHERE/RETURNING references a column; `UPDATE t SET tenant=$1` or WHERE true leaks 100/100 (17.11 and 19rc1)
nodes.summary: PG applies SELECT policy to the new row when the UPDATE reads columns, acting as implicit WITH CHECK; policy-free statements (no column refs) lose that. Any lowering that always emits `tenant = $1` conjunct hides the misconfig in tests. Good policy (USING=WITH CHECK) 0 leaks; split policies without WITH CHECK default to USING 0 leaks; owner without FORCE 110/300 leak, FORCE 0.
nodes.specifics: dbg2.sql, wp_results3.json; docs say 'check new row [a]' only if read access required; consistent but easy to miss
nodes.overclaim_risk: misconfig scenario, not an engine bug
nodes.underclaim_risk: CI must test RLS policies with column-free writes

nodes.title: ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE ... WHERE f(t.col) runs a non-leakproof function on another tenant's row before RLS USING errors (17.11 and 19rc1 executed); DO SELECT via views leaks rows (19rc1)
nodes.summary: Executed: peek() NOTICE 'saw secretB' for tenant a under good RLS in ExecOnConflictUpdate (master source: lock row, visibility, evaluate ON CONFLICT WHERE, then WCO_RLS_CONFLICT_CHECK). Plain UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE WHERE peek see only own rows. Contradicts docs claim that policy exprs run before user quals except leakproof. pgsql-hackers 2026-09-25 thread (shihao zhong; Viktor Holmberg reports same WHERE-bypass for PG18) open; PG19rc1 DO SELECT on security_barrier view returned the hidden row (executed), plain view too (Kirill Reshke); RLS itself safe for DO SELECT (ERROR).

nodes.title: SQLite: authorizer deny SQLITE_DELETE does not stop REPLACE's implicit deletes (261/300 leaks; control: plain DELETE denied); update_hook not called, change counter not incremented
nodes.summary: Authorizer is prepare-time only per docs; REPLACE deletes pre-existing rows, delete triggers only with recursive_triggers (default off). Authorizer deny UPDATE t.x does block DO UPDATE but statically (all 300 incl legit). Hardening: refuse REPLACE/OR REPLACE/UPDATE OR REPLACE in adapter; composite PK; also note SQLite has no RLS, so PEP in server is the only gate.
nodes.underclaim_risk: docs say behavior may change in future release

nodes.title: Redis/Valkey write path: hex-id prefix + ACL ~t:{A}:* gives 0/29 mutation leaks; raw ids with glob metachars give 13-15/29 (a*, a?), 5/29 (a[b-c], backslash); +@all FLUSHDB/SWAPDB leak; SCAN/RANDOMKEY leak foreign key names
nodes.summary: valkey 9.1.2 (redis_version 7.2.4 compat) and redis 8.10.2 identical. ACL checks both keys of RENAME/COPY/SMOVE/LMOVE (NOPERM); SORT BY/GET denied for key-restricted users; EVAL undeclared key blocked by script ACL; MOVE own key to db1 allowed. Docs now state key patterns do not limit FLUSHALL/FLUSHDB/SWAPDB. Read-leak: SCAN without MATCH returns foreign key names on both; RANDOMKEY sometimes; KEYS * unless denied.

nodes.title: L5: write-path unsound-construct denylist + mandated hardened forms
nodes.summary: Never lower to: (1) INSERT..ON CONFLICT/REPLACE/MERGE on a key lacking tenant in arbiter; mandated: composite (tenant,id) or DO UPDATE WHERE t.tenant=excluded.tenant, no user expr in that WHERE; (2) INSERT OR REPLACE/REPLACE INTO/UPDATE OR REPLACE (SQLite) and ON DUPLICATE KEY on multi-unique tables; (3) SET lists containing tenant col or PK; (4) data-modifying CTEs, MERGE NOT MATCHED BY SOURCE, ON CONFLICT DO SELECT; (5) UPDATE/DELETE without literal tenant conjunct relying on RLS alone; (6) schemas with non tenant-scoped or SECURITY DEFINER triggers/FK actions; (7) RLS policies lacking explicit WITH CHECK or without FORCE for owner roles; CI test must run column-free writes; (8) Redis: raw tenant ids in key/ACL patterns, +@all without -flushall -flushdb -swapdb -keys -scan-without-match, RENAME/COPY/MOVE cross-prefix, EVAL/FUNCTION/SORT; (9) uniform error for unique violation on foreign key.

nodes.title: Native enforcement catch matrix: PG RLS (good ALL policy) catches every cross-tenant write case; sqlite authorizer partial; Redis ACL catches key-bearing commands but not keyspace-wide ones
nodes.summary: RLS good: 0 leaks over U2, UP1/2, C1/C2, M1, P2, T1 invoker; fails: owner no FORCE (110/300), SECURITY DEFINER trigger (127/300), CHECK(true)+column-free write (100/100), ON CONFLICT WHERE peek. Answers R-DB-7: write path is closed for PG iff composite arbiter + RLS FORCE + explicit WITH CHECK + vetted triggers; open for SQLite without custom PEP.
